objective: The owner's request of 2026-11-24 (sub-goal B317, assumption A223; goals G15 with G17 and G18): the fold of emergence, a made pattern that reads another pattern and grows its own. Under every law studied so far, parts of the live roster that have come apart act alone for ever, which is why the parts that copy themselves are a population and not a machine. Find whether there is a growth law under which parts that have come apart can meet again, so that what one part builds depends on whether another part is there. First step: read what the record's studies of a birth that takes a distinction already shared found (rule R, assumption A230; rule Q, A235; the move of A225), including where rule R re-reads in the wrong places; then run those laws on the ring that returns and on the two-knot part that copies itself. The test: run each start twice, once with the second part present and once without it; a part reads another when its course differs between the two runs. Standard: a frozen pre-registration reviewed cold by the advisor; an engine written from the frozen text and checked against the existing ones; the knot test on every knot made, under parity and not-all-equal; every added rule named as a scaffold and swapped before anything is claimed about the model; no claims about living things or minds. Stop at one part whose course depends on another, or at a reason this cannot happen under these laws. If a part does read another, say plainly whether the reader was supplied by hand or made by the growth.
title: Parts that meet again: does what one part builds depend on whether another part is there?
